nodes.name: SiO2 nanospheres synthesis
nodes.procedure: 36 mL deionized water and 104 mL ethanol were mixed, then 6 mL TEOS was dropped into the mixed solution and agitated for 10 min. Subsequently, 8 mL ammonia was also dropped into in the above solution and kept stirring over 6 h. The resulting white emulsion was centrifuged and washed with deionized water for three times, and then freeze-dried.

nodes.name: ZIF-67@SiO2 synthesis
nodes.procedure: 1.2 g SiO2 nanospheres were dispersed in 12.5 mL methanol solution and sonicated for 30 min. Then 3 mmol Co(NO3)2·6H2O was added and kept stirring for 20 min. 12 mmol 2-MeIm was added in 12.5 mL methanol solution and quickly poured into above pink solution, then stirred at 80°C until methanol solution evaporated completely. Finally, the purple powder was obtained and ground for further use.
nodes.source_text: 2.3 Synthesis of ZIF-67@SiO2... ground for further use.

nodes.name: Co@HNC synthesis
nodes.procedure: The purple powder was placed in porcelain boat and subjected to pyrolysis at 800°C under N2 atmosphere at 2°C/min for 2 h. After natural cooling, the acquired black foam-like product was added in 3 M KOH aqueous solution and kept 70°C for 2 h to remove SiO2 template, and the powder was denoted as Co@HNC.

nodes.name: CoP@HNC phosphorization
nodes.procedure: Co@HNC was pretreated in muffle furnace, and heated to 300°C with 5°C/min for 15 min. Subsequently, 500 mg NaH2PO2 and 50 mg pretreated Co@HNC were put in two porcelain boats, respectively, then transferred to tube furnace with NaH2PO2 placing at the upstream side. The tube furnace was ramped up to 300°C at 2°C/min and CoP@HNC was obtained after 2 h.

nodes.source_text: the CoP@HNC displays fascinating EMW absorption properties with lower reflection loss (RL) value of −60.8 dB and absorption bandwidth as wide as 4.96 GHz ... nodes.characterization_summary: CoP@HNC shows peaks at 31.6°, 36.6°, 48.4°, 56.4° corresponding to (011), (111), (211), (301) planes of CoP (PDF 29-0497); Co@NC shows peaks at 44.3°, 51.6°, 75.9° for fcc Co (111), (200), (220).
nodes.evidence_snippet: While the CoP@HNC composites display five peaks at 31.6°, 36.6°, 48.4°, 56.4°, belonging to (011), (111), (211), and (301) crystal planes of the formed CoP nanoparticles, respectively (PDF no. 29-0497).

nodes.characterization_summary: CoP@HNC exhibits type-IV hysteresis indicating mesopores, specific surface area 509.91 m²/g (2.55× Co@NC), pore sizes 4.2-6.4 nm; Co@NC 200.03 m²/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with Co@NC (200.03 m²/g), the resultant CoP@HNC (509.91 m²/g) exhibits larger specific surface area (2.55 times than that of Co@NC)... The pore-sizes distribution mainly concentrated around 4.2 - 6.4 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoP@HNC shows honeycomb-like porous architecture with 300 nm macropores and rough surface after phosphorization; Co@HNC shows smooth curved honeycomb structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After removing the template, the remaining Co@HNC displays honeycomb-like porous architecture with uniformly dispersed spherical macropores with pore size of around 300 nm... After in situ phosphorization-treated process, CoP@HNC displays rough surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoP@HNC shows uniform 300 nm pores with evenly distributed CoP nanoparticles; HRTEM reveals 0.189 nm (211) CoP lattice fringe and 0.34 nm graphitic carbon shell.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM characterizations further demonstrate uniform circular dispersion in the porous carbon matrix with a diameter of 300 nm... Figure 2(f) displays the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image of CoP@HNC, showing 0.189 nm lattice fringe corresponding to the (211) facet of CoP phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoP@HNC shows 0.189 nm lattice fringe for CoP (211) and 0.34 nm graphitic carbon (002) with lattice mismatch at heterogeneous interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2(f) displays the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image of CoP@HNC, showing 0.189 nm lattice fringe corresponding to the (211) facet of CoP phase... Meanwhile, the CoP nanoparticles are embedded in internal layers of graphitic carbon shell with crystal plane of 0.34 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoP@HNC shows homogeneous distribution of Co, P, N, C elements with Co:P atomic ratio ≈1:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with Co@HNC, the corresponding EDS elemental mapping of CoP@HNC composites demonstrates that Co, P, N, and C elements are homogeneously distributed throughout the matrix... Additionally, the spectrum shows that the atomic ratios of Co and P are close to 1:1.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoP@HNC ID/IG=0.99 (higher defects than Co@HNC 0.93, Co@NC 0.91) with D band 1343 cm⁻¹, G band 1589 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3(a), two noticeable peaks at 1,343 and 1,589 cm⁻¹ are assigned to the D band and G band, respectively. For Co@NC and Co@HNC composites, the intensity ratios of ID/IG are 0.91 and 0.93, respectively... The value of ID/IG for CoP@HNC is 0.99.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoP@HNC shows Co 2p Co-P peaks at 778.82 eV (2p3/2) and 794 eV (2p1/2), oxidized Co at 781.81 eV and 797.63 eV (positive shift 0.4-0.63 eV vs Co@NC); P 2p at 129.5 eV (2p3/2) and 130.4 eV (2p1/2); N 1s and C 1s show negative shift indicating electron transfer from CoP to N-doped carbon.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For 2p3/2 and 2p1/2 peaks of CoP@HNC, the peaks at 778.82 and 794 eV, and 781.81 and 797.63 eV, are assigned to Co-P and oxidized Co species, respectively. Obviously, both of the Co 2p3/2 and Co 2p1/2 species of CoP@HNC show a positive peak shift of 0.4 and 0.63 eV to higher binding energy than Co@NC... Compared with Co 2p, the peaks of N 1s and C 1s display a negative shift to low binding energy... Figure 3(f) displays the P 2p spectrum in CoP@HNC, where two signals of P 2p3/2 (129.5 eV) and P 2p1/2 (130.4 eV) can be obtained.

nodes.characterization_summary: N-doped carbon in CoP@HNC shows positive slope indicating n-type semiconductor with flat band potential -0.85 V vs Ag/AgCl.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Mott-Schottky plot demonstrates that N-doped carbon belongs to N-type semiconductor because of the positive slope and corresponding flat band is -0.85 V vs. Ag/AgCl.

nodes.characterization_summary: N-doped carbon in CoP@HNC shows work function 6.57 eV (Ecutoff 14.65 eV), valence band maximum 3.42 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For N-doped carbon, the cut off edge (Ecutoff) and the Fermi level (EF) are 14.65 and 0 eV, respectively, and the work function is 6.57 eV which can be obtained by the formula: Φ = 21.22 - (Ecutoff - EF)... In addition, the top of valence-band and Fermi-level is 1.62 eV, thus the top of valence-band is around 3.42 eV.
